articles.title: 完形填空 · 有耐心的父母如何示范情绪控制
articles.context: 文章讨论耐心型教养：父母难免疲惫失控，但持续练习冷静和情绪控制，既保护亲子关系，也为孩子示范终身受用的能力。
rows: Being a good parent is what every parent would like to be.
成为一个好父母，是每一位父母都希望做到的事。
advance
But defining what it means to be a good parent is undoubtedly very tricky, particularly since children respond differently to the same style of parenting.
但要界定“好父母”究竟意味着什么，无疑非常棘手，尤其是因为不同孩子对同一种教养方式的反应并不相同。
contrast
A calm, rule-following child might respond better to a different sort of parenting than, for example, a younger one.
例如，一个安静守规矩的孩子和一个更年幼的孩子，可能更适合不同的教养方式。
example
Fortunately, there's another sort of parent that's easier to describe: a patient parent.
幸运的是，还有一种父母更容易描述：有耐心的父母。
advance
Children of every age benefit from patient parenting.
各个年龄段的孩子都能从耐心的教养中受益。
explain
Still, while every parent would like to be patient, this is no easy task.
不过，尽管每位父母都想保持耐心，这却绝不是一件容易的事。
contrast
Sometimes, parents get exhausted and are unable to maintain a tolerant style with their kids.
有时父母会精疲力竭，无法继续以宽容的方式对待孩子。
example
I understand this.
这一点我完全理解。
settle
You're only human, and sometimes your kids can push you just a little too far.
你毕竟只是普通人，有时孩子确实会把你逼得有些过头。
story
And then the inevitable happens: You lose your patience and either scream at your kids or say something that was too harsh and does nobody any good.
随后，不可避免的事情发生了：你失去耐心，要么冲孩子大吼，要么说出过于严厉、对谁都没有好处的话。
action_turn
You wish that you could turn back the clock and start over.
你恨不得让时钟倒转，一切重新来过。
resolve
We've all been there.
这种时刻我们都经历过。
settle
However, even though it's common, it's vital to keep in mind that in a single moment of fatigue, you can say something to your child that you may regret for a long time.
然而，即使这种情况很常见，也必须牢记：一次疲惫中的失言，就可能让你说出今后很长时间都会后悔的话。
warning
This may not only do damage to your relationship with your child but also affect your child's self-esteem.
这不仅可能损害你与孩子的关系，还会影响孩子的自尊。
conclude
If you consistently lose your cool with your kids, then you are modeling a lack of emotional control for your kids.
如果你总是在孩子面前失去冷静，那么你实际上是在向他们示范缺乏情绪控制的样子。
warning
We are all becoming increasingly aware of the importance of modeling patience for the younger generation.
我们越来越意识到，为年轻一代示范耐心有多么重要。
explain
This is a skill that will help them all throughout life.
这是一项能让他们终身受益的技能。
conclude
In fact, the ability to maintain emotional control when confronted by stress is one of the most significant of all life's skills.
事实上，在面对压力时仍能保持情绪控制，是人生最重要的能力之一。
emphasize
Certainly, it's hard to maintain patience at all times with your kids.
当然，要始终对孩子保持耐心很难。
qualify
A more practical goal is to try to be as calm as you can when faced with trying situations involving your children.
更实际的目标，是在面对与孩子有关的棘手处境时，尽量让自己保持冷静。
resolve
I can promise you this: As a result of working toward this goal, you and your children will benefit and emerge from stressful moments feeling better physically and emotionally.
我可以向你保证：只要朝这个目标努力，你和孩子都会从中受益，并能以更好的身心状态走出那些压力时刻。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 老鼠会把社交机器人当成伙伴吗
articles.context: 研究人员让真实老鼠与社交型、非社交型机器人共同生活，发现老鼠更愿意帮助曾与自己互动的社交机器人，说明简单的行为线索也足以触发社会性回应。
rows: Rats and other animals need to be highly attuned to social signals from others so they can identify friends to cooperate with and enemies to avoid.
老鼠和其他动物需要对同类发出的社会信号高度敏锐，才能识别可以合作的朋友和应当避开的敌人。
explain
To find out if this extends to non-living beings, Laleh Quinn at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats.
为了弄清这种能力是否也会延伸到非生命体，加州大学圣迭戈分校的拉莱·奎因及其同事测试了老鼠能否识别机器鼠发出的社会信号。
report
They housed eight adult rats with two types of robotic rat—one social and one asocial—for four days.
他们让八只成年老鼠与两种机器鼠共同生活了四天：一种具有社交行为，另一种则没有。
sequence
The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels to move around and colourful markings.
这些机器鼠的设计相当极简，看起来像更厚实的电脑鼠标，装有轮子可以移动，并带有彩色标记。
explain
During the experiment, the social robot rat followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors to let trapped rats escape.
实验期间，社交型机器鼠会跟随真实老鼠活动，和它们玩同样的玩具，还会打开笼门放出被困的老鼠。
sequence
Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side.
与此同时，非社交型机器鼠只会前后、左右移动。
contrast
Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever.
接着，研究人员把机器鼠关进笼子，并让真实老鼠有机会通过按下杠杆将它们放出。
sequence
Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 per cent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one.
在每种条件各18次试验中，真实老鼠释放社交型机器鼠的平均可能性比释放非社交型机器鼠高52%。
statistic
This suggests that the rats perceived the social robot as a genuine social being.
这表明，老鼠把社交型机器鼠视为真正的社会性存在。
conclude
They may have bonded more with the social robot because it displayed behaviors like communal exploring and playing.
它们可能与社交型机器鼠建立了更强的联系，因为后者表现出了共同探索、一起玩耍等行为。
explain
This could lead to the rats better remembering having freed it earlier, and wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped, says Quinn.
奎因说，这可能使老鼠更清楚地记得自己先前曾救过它，并期待自己被困时机器鼠也能回报这一帮助。
explain_quote

“Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity—where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them,” says Quinn.
奎因说：“研究已经证明，老鼠会进行多种形式的互惠帮助与合作，其中包括所谓的直接互惠——一只老鼠会帮助此前帮助过自己的另一只老鼠。”
dialogue
The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design.
考虑到机器鼠设计如此简单，真实老鼠竟如此愿意与社交型机器鼠建立关系，令人意外。
contrast
The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels.
这台机器人与普通老鼠大小相当，却只是一个装着轮子的简单塑料盒。
explain

“We'd assumed we'd have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn't necessary,” says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
参与研究的澳大利亚昆士兰大学珍妮特·怀尔斯说：“我们原以为必须给它装上会动的头和尾巴、面部特征，还要加上气味，让它闻起来像真老鼠，但事实证明没有必要。”
dialogue
The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots.
这一发现表明，老鼠对社会性线索十分敏感，即便这些线索来自最简单的机器人。
conclude
Similarly, children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings, even when they display only simple social signals.
类似地，即使机器人只表现出简单的社会信号，儿童也往往会把它们当作同伴来对待。
compare
“We humans seem to be fascinated by robots, and it turns out other animals are too,” says Wiles.
怀尔斯说：“我们人类似乎会被机器人吸引，而事实证明，其他动物也是如此。”
dialogue

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 为什么顶级 CEO 薪酬持续上涨
articles.context: 文章为高管高薪提供经济学解释：顶级企业机会扩张而顶级CEO人才稀缺，岗位所需能力也更复杂；治理更严格却薪酬仍上升，作者据此认为高薪并不能简单归因于内部掠夺。
rows: It is true that CEO pay has gone up—top ones may make 300 times the pay of typical workers on average, and since the mid-1970s, CEO pay for large publicly traded American corporations has, by varying estimates, gone up by about 500%.
CEO薪酬确实上涨了：顶尖CEO的平均收入可能达到普通员工的300倍；不同估算显示，自20世纪70年代中期以来，美国大型上市公司CEO的薪酬大约上涨了500%。
statistic
The typical CEO of a top American corporation now makes about $18.9 million a year.
如今，美国顶级公司的典型CEO年收入约为1890万美元。
statistic
The best model for understanding the growth of CEO pay is that of limited CEO talent in a world where business opportunities for the top firms are growing rapidly.
理解CEO薪酬增长的最好模型，是在顶级企业商业机会迅速扩张的世界里，真正优秀的CEO人才却十分有限。
explain
The efforts of America's highest-earning 1% have been one of the more dynamic elements of the global economy.
美国收入最高的1%人群所作的努力，一直是全球经济中更具活力的因素之一。
explain
It's not popular to say, but one reason their pay has gone up so much is that CEOs really have upped their game relative to many other workers in the U.S. economy.
这种说法可能不讨喜，但CEO薪酬大幅上涨的一个原因，是与美国经济中的许多其他劳动者相比，他们确实提升了自身能力。
contrast
Today's CEO, at least for major American firms, must have many more skills than simply being able to “run the company.”
如今的CEO，至少在美国大型企业中，所需技能远不只是“把公司经营起来”。
explain
CEOs must have a good sense of financial markets and maybe even how the company should trade in them.
CEO必须对金融市场有良好判断，甚至还要懂得公司应当如何参与其中的交易。
explain
They also need better public relations skills than their predecessors, as the costs of even a minor slipup can be significant.
他们还需要比前任更强的公共关系能力，因为哪怕一个小小失误，代价也可能很大。
explain
Then there's the fact that large American companies are much more globalized than ever before, with supply chains spread across a larger number of countries.
此外，美国大型企业如今比以往任何时候都更加全球化，供应链分布在更多国家。
explain
To lead in that system requires knowledge that is fairly mind-boggling.
要领导这样一个体系，需要掌握的知识之多几乎令人难以想象。
emphasize
Plus, virtually all major American companies are becoming tech companies, often with their own research and development.
而且，几乎所有美国大型企业都在变成科技企业，往往还拥有自己的研发体系。
explain
And beyond this, major CEOs still have to do all the day-to-day work they have always done.
除此之外，大公司CEO还必须完成他们历来承担的所有日常工作。
conclude
The common idea that high CEO pay is mainly about ripping people off doesn't explain history very well.
把CEO高薪主要解释成对他人的盘剥，这种常见观点并不能很好解释历史。
contrast
By most measures, corporate governance has become a lot tighter and more rigorous since the 1970s.
按大多数衡量标准，自20世纪70年代以来，公司治理已经变得更加严密和严格。
report
Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising.
然而，恰恰主要是在治理不断加强的这一时期，CEO薪酬一直居高不下并持续上涨。
contrast
That suggests it is in the broader corporate interest to recruit top candidates for increasingly tough jobs.
这说明，为越来越艰难的职位招募顶尖人才，符合公司的整体利益。
conclude

Furthermore, the highest CEO salaries are paid to outside candidates, not to the cozy insider picks, another sign that high CEO pay is not some kind of depredation at the expense of the rest of the company.
此外，最高的CEO薪酬往往付给外部候选人，而不是关系亲密的内部人选；这再次表明，高额CEO薪酬并不是以公司其他成员为代价的某种掠夺。
explain
And the stock market reacts positively when companies tie CEO pay to, say, stock prices, a sign that those practices build up corporate value not just for the CEO.
而当公司把CEO薪酬与股价等指标挂钩时，股票市场会作出积极反应，这说明此类做法提升的是公司价值，而不只是CEO个人的利益。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 城市限行无法独自解决空气污染
articles.context: 文章以马德里清洁空气区政策反复为例，批评欧洲依赖城市各自限行的碎片化治理：成本被转嫁给司机，而汽车制造商和国家政府应承担更大责任。
rows: Madrid was hailed as a public health guiding light last November when it rolled out ambitious restrictions on the most polluting cars.
去年11月，马德里推出针对污染最严重车辆的雄心勃勃的限制措施，一度被誉为公共卫生治理的榜样。
story
Seven months and one election day later, a new conservative city council suspended enforcement of the clean air zone, a first step toward its possible termination.
七个月并经历一次选举之后，新上台的保守派市议会暂停执行清洁空气区规定，这可能是最终取消该政策的第一步。
contrast
Mayor Jose Luis Martinez-Almeida made opposition to the zone a centrepiece of his election campaign, despite its success in improving air quality.
尽管该区域已经成功改善空气质量，市长何塞·路易斯·马丁内斯-阿尔梅达仍把反对它作为竞选活动的核心议题。
explain
A judge has now overruled the city's decision to stop levying fines, ordering them restored.
如今，一名法官推翻了市政府停止罚款的决定，要求恢复处罚。
story
But with legal battles ahead, the zone's future looks uncertain at best.
但随着法律争端继续，其前景充其量只能说是不确定。
conclude
Madrid's back and forth on clean air is a pointed reminder of the limits to the patchwork, city-by-city approach that characterises efforts on air pollution across Europe, Britain very much included.
马德里在清洁空气政策上的反复，鲜明提醒我们：欧洲包括英国在内，以城市为单位、零散拼接式治理空气污染的方法存在明显局限。
explain
Among other weaknesses, the measures cities must employ when left to tackle dirty air on their own are politically controversial, and therefore vulnerable.
诸多弱点之一是，当城市被迫独自处理空气污染时，它们采用的措施往往具有政治争议，因此十分脆弱。
warning

That's because they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers—who must pay fees or buy better vehicles—rather than on to the car manufacturers whose cheating is the real cause of our toxic pollution.
这是因为，这些措施不可避免地把净化空气的成本压在个人司机身上——他们要缴费或购买更好的车辆——而不是让那些作弊、并真正造成有毒污染的汽车制造商承担成本。
explain
It's not hard to imagine a similar reversal happening in London.
不难想象，类似的政策逆转也可能发生在伦敦。
example
The new ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) is likely to be a big issue in next year's mayoral election.
新的超低排放区很可能成为明年市长选举中的重要议题。
report

And if Sadiq Khan wins and extends it to the North and South Circular roads in 2021 as he intends, it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
如果萨迪克·汗获胜，并按计划在2021年把该区域扩展到北、南环路，那么届时受影响的大量司机势必会激烈反对。
warning
It's not that measures such as London's Ulez are useless.
这并不是说伦敦超低排放区之类的措施毫无用处。
qualify
Far from it.
恰恰相反。
emphasize
Local officials are using the levers that are available to them to safeguard residents' health in the face of a serious threat.
面对严重威胁，地方官员正在利用手中可用的政策工具保护居民健康。
explain
The zones do deliver some improvements to air quality, and the science tells us that means real health benefits.
这些区域确实能改善一定程度的空气质量，而科学告诉我们，这意味着真实的健康收益。
conclude
But mayors and councilors can only do so much about a problem that is far bigger than any one city or town.
但面对一个远超任何单一城市或城镇规模的问题，市长和议员能做的终究有限。
contrast
They are acting because national governments—Britain's and others across Europe—have failed to do so.
他们之所以采取行动，是因为英国以及欧洲其他国家的中央政府没有尽到责任。
explain

Restrictions that keep highly polluting cars out of certain areas—city centres, “school streets”, even individual roads—are a response to the absence of a larger effort to properly enforce existing regulations and require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance.
禁止高污染汽车进入市中心、“学校街道”乃至个别道路等限制措施，是在更大规模行动缺位时的应对办法；本应采取的行动，是切实执行现有规定，并要求汽车企业使车辆达到合规标准。
explain
Wales has introduced special low speed limits to minimise pollution.
威尔士已经实行特殊低速限速，以尽量减少污染。
example
We're doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars.
我们几乎什么都做了，唯独没有坚持要求制造商把汽车变得更清洁。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · Z 世代求职更看重确定性与稳定
articles.context: 文章分析即将进入职场的Z世代：他们成长于2008年金融危机并背负高额学贷，因此比千禧一代更务实谨慎，尤其重视就业安全、稳定与可预见的未来。
rows: Now that members of Generation Z are graduating college this spring—the most commonly-accepted definition says this generation was born after 1995, give or take a year—the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks.
随着Z世代成员在今年春天大学毕业——最常见的定义认为这一代人大约出生于1995年以后——近几周公众对他们的关注持续升温。
advance
Gen Zs are about to hit the streets looking for work in a labor market that's tighter than it's been in decades.
Z世代即将在一个数十年来最紧俏的劳动力市场中开始求职。
story

And employers are planning on hiring about 17 percent more new graduates for jobs in the U.S. this year than last, according to a survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers.
美国全国高校与雇主协会的一项调查显示，今年雇主计划招聘的美国应届毕业生比去年多约17%。
statistic
Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them.
人人都想知道，这些即将坐进空置办公隔间的年轻人与前辈会有何不同。
ask
If “entitled” is the most common adjective, fairly or not, applied to millennials (those born between 1981 and 1995), the catchwords for Generation Z are practical and cautious.
如果说“自我中心”——无论公不公平——是最常被用来形容千禧一代（1981至1995年出生）的话，那么Z世代的关键词则是务实和谨慎。
compare
According to the career counselors and experts who study them, Generation Zs are clear-eyed, economic pragmatists.
研究他们的职业顾问和专家认为，Z世代头脑清醒，是经济上的实用主义者。
explain
Despite graduating into the best economy in the past 50 years, Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like.
尽管毕业时遇上过去50年来最好的经济环境，Z世代却很清楚经济灾难是什么样子。
contrast
They were impressionable kids during the crash of 2008, when many of their parents lost their jobs or their life savings or both.
2008年金融危机发生时，他们正处在容易受影响的童年阶段，当时许多人的父母失去了工作、毕生积蓄，或两者兼失。
story
They aren't interested in taking any chances.
他们并不愿意冒险。
emphasize
The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency, especially for those who have college debt.
经济繁荣似乎并没有多少作用去缓解这一代人深层的焦虑和紧迫感，尤其是对那些背负大学债务的人而言。
contrast
College loan balances in the U.S. now stand at a record $1.5 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve.
美联储数据显示，美国大学贷款余额如今达到创纪录的1.5万亿美元。
statistic
One survey from Accenture found that 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind.
埃森哲的一项调查发现，今年88%的毕业班学生在选择专业时就考虑到了未来工作。
statistic

In a 2019 survey of University of Georgia students, meanwhile, the career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose).
与此同时，佐治亚大学就业办公室2019年的一项学生调查发现，未来雇主最受看重的特质是能够提供有保障的就业，其后依次是职业发展与培训，以及鼓舞人心的使命感。
report

Job security or stability was the second most important career goal (work-life balance was number one), followed by a sense of being dedicated to a cause or to feel good about serving the greater good.
工作安全或稳定是第二重要的职业目标（第一是工作与生活平衡），其后是投身某项事业的使命感，或因服务更大的公共利益而产生的满足感。
explain
That's a big change from the previous generation.
与上一代相比，这是一个很大的变化。
contrast

“Millennials wanted more flexibility in their lives,” notes Tanya Michelsen, Associate Director of YouthSight, a UK-based brand manager that conducts regular 60-day surveys of British youth, in findings that might just as well apply to American youth.
总部位于英国、定期对英国年轻人开展60天调查的品牌管理机构YouthSight副主任塔尼娅·米克尔森指出：“千禧一代希望生活中有更多灵活性。”这一发现同样可能适用于美国年轻人。
dialogue
“Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability, because of the rise of the gig economy.
“由于零工经济兴起，Z世代正在寻求更多确定性和稳定。
dialogue
They have trouble seeing a financial future and they are quite risk averse.”
他们很难看清自己的财务未来，因此相当厌恶风险。”
dialogue

articles.title: 阅读 Part B · 在办公室赢得所有人的五种方法
articles.context: 文章给出改善办公室人际关系的五种做法：适度坦诚、耐心倾听、拓展同事网络、真诚赞美，以及根据不同对象调整沟通方式。
rows: Is it possible to like everyone in your office?
有可能喜欢办公室里的每一个人吗？
ask
Think about how tough it is to get together 15 people, much less 50, who all get along perfectly.
想想看，让15个人相处得完全融洽已经多么困难，更不用说50个人。
explain
But unlike in friendships, you need coworkers.
但与朋友关系不同，你离不开同事。
contrast
You work with them every day, and you depend on them just as they depend on you.
你每天都和他们一起工作，你依赖他们，正如他们依赖你。
explain
Here are some ways that you can get the whole office on your side.
下面这些方法，可以帮助你赢得整个办公室的支持。
advance
If you have a bone to pick with someone in your workplace, you may try to stay tight-lipped around them.
如果你对工作中的某个人心有不满，可能会选择在他面前守口如瓶。
story
But you won't be helping either one of you.
但这样做对你们双方都没有帮助。
contrast
A Harvard Business School study found that observers consistently rated those who were frank about themselves more highly, while those who hid lost trustworthiness.
哈佛商学院的一项研究发现，观察者一直会给那些坦率谈论自己的人更高评价，而有所隐瞒的人会失去可信度。
report
The lesson is not that you should make your personal life an open book, but rather, when given the option to offer up details about yourself or painstakingly conceal them, you should just be honest.
这并不是要你把私人生活完全公开，而是说，当你可以选择透露自己的信息或费力掩饰时，最好坦诚一些。
conclude
Just as important as being honest about yourself is being receptive to others.
和坦诚面对自己同样重要的，是愿意倾听他人。
compare
We often feel the need to tell others how we feel, whether it's a concern about a project, a stray thought, or a compliment.
我们常常觉得有必要告诉别人自己的感受，无论是对项目的担忧、偶然冒出的想法，还是一句赞美。
explain
Those are all valid, but you need to take time to hear out your coworkers, too.
这些表达都很合理，但你也需要花时间把同事的话听完。
contrast
In fact, rushing to get your own ideas out there can cause colleagues to feel you don't value their opinions.
事实上，急着抛出自己的想法，可能会让同事觉得你不重视他们的意见。
warning
Do your best to engage coworkers in a genuine, back-and-forth conversation, rather than prioritizing your own thoughts.
尽量与同事进行真正有来有往的交流，而不是总把自己的想法放在最前面。
conclude
It's common to have a “cubicle mate” or special confidant in a work setting.
在职场中，有一个“隔间搭档”或特别知己很常见。
story
But in addition to those trusted coworkers, you should expand your horizons and find out about all the people around you.
但除了这些值得信赖的同事，你还应拓宽视野，去了解身边更多的人。
advance
Use your lunch and coffee breaks to meet up with colleagues you don't always see.
利用午餐和咖啡休息时间，去见见那些平时不常碰面的同事。
encourage
Find out about their lives and interests beyond the job.
了解他们工作之外的生活和兴趣。
encourage
It requires minimal effort and goes a long way.
这几乎不费什么力气，却能带来很大效果。
emphasize
This will help to grow your internal network, in addition to being a nice break in the work day.
这样既能扩大你在公司内部的人际网络，也能让工作日得到一次愉快的调剂。
conclude
Positive feedback is important for anyone to hear.
对任何人来说，听到积极反馈都很重要。
explain
And you don't have to be someone's boss to tell them they did an exceptional job on a particular project.
你不必是某人的上司，也可以告诉他某个项目完成得非常出色。
encourage
This will help engender good will in others.
这会帮助你在他人心中产生好感。
conclude
But don't overdo it or be fake about it.
但不要夸过头，也不要虚情假意。
warning
One study found that people responded best to comments that shifted from negative to positive, possibly because it suggested they had won somebody over.
一项研究发现，人们对由负面转向正面的评价反应最好，可能因为这意味着他们已经赢得了某个人的认可。
report
This one may be a bit more difficult to pull off, but it can go a long way to achieving results.
这一点做起来也许更难，但对于取得理想结果非常有效。
qualify
Remember in dealing with any coworker what they appreciate from an interaction.
和任何同事打交道时，都要记住对方希望从互动中得到什么。
encourage
Watch out for how they verbalize with others.
留意他们与别人说话的方式。
explain
Some people like small talk in a meeting before digging into important matters, while others are more straightforward.
有些人喜欢在会议中先闲聊几句，再进入重要议题；另一些人则更加直接。
compare
Jokes that work on one person won't necessarily land with another.
对一个人奏效的玩笑，对另一个人未必有效。
contrast
So, adapt your style accordingly to type.
因此，要根据不同类型的人相应调整自己的沟通风格。
resolve
Consider the person that you're dealing with in advance and what will get you to your desired outcome.
提前想一想你将面对的是怎样的人，以及怎样做才能得到你想要的结果。
conclude

articles.title: 翻译 · 失败取决于我们如何看待它
articles.context: 文章把失败重新定义为学习机会：失败能帮助人成长、避免重犯错误，也能让人认识自己的力量、真正的朋友以及意外的成功动力。
rows: It's almost impossible to go through life without experiencing some kind of failure.
人的一生几乎不可能完全不经历某种失败。
explain
But, the wonderful thing about failure is that it's entirely up to us to decide how to look at it.
但失败有一点很奇妙：如何看待它，完全由我们自己决定。
contrast
We can choose to see failure as “the end of the world.”
我们可以选择把失败看成“世界末日”。
contrast
Or, we can look at failure as the incredible learning experience that it often is.
也可以把失败看成它常常真正具有的价值——一次极其宝贵的学习经历。
contrast
Every time we fail at something, we can choose to look for the lesson we're meant to learn.
每当某件事失败，我们都可以选择去寻找自己应该从中学到的教训。
explain
These lessons are very important; they're how we grow, and how we keep from making that same mistake again.
这些教训非常重要；我们正是借此成长，也借此避免再次犯下同样的错误。
explain
Failures stop us only if we let them.
只有当我们任由失败阻挡自己时，它才真正能让我们停下脚步。
conclude
Failure can also teach us things about ourselves that we would never have learned otherwise.
失败还会让我们认识自己身上一些原本永远不会发现的东西。
advance
For instance, failure can help you discover how strong a person you are.
例如，失败能帮助你发现自己究竟有多坚强。
example
Failing at something can help you discover your truest friends, or help you find unexpected motivation to succeed.
一件事的失败可以帮你认清谁是最真诚的朋友，也可能让你找到意想不到的成功动力。
conclude
